title: Can a number be less than zero?
description: A tall block of floors stands with a ground line across it. Some floors sit above the line and some below it, and no number is written on any floor. The video ends on the open question of whether a number can be less than zero.
teaching_notes: One idea: some places lie below the ground, so the ground floor may not be where numbers stop. Ask children what they would call a floor under the ground, and do not confirm any name, because the next topic settles it. Watch for students who say there is nothing below zero.

source: Can a number be less than zero?
video_script.why: Before any negative number, the child sees floors below the ground and wonders whether a number can be less than zero.
video_script.substitution: Picture a tall block of floors with a ground line, and ask whether a number can be less than zero.
video_script.anchor: Ruhee, the tall block of floors built by Leeza, with floors above and below the ground line

names.Leeza: owner of the ice cream factory who built the multi-storey block of attractions
names.Ruhee: the multi-storey block of floors above and below the ground, used as the model for integers

hold_back: the number for a floor below the ground
maths_rules: A tall block with a ground line is shown, with floors above the line and floors below it.
The entrance is at the ground floor, called the Welcome Hall in the book.
No floor number and no sign is written anywhere.
The open question: can a number be less than zero, and how would we write it. It is never answered.
video_script.design: One idea: there is a side of zero below it. Assumes nothing. Wrong idea: none is broken. Transitions: the pictures arrive one by one and all stay to the end; no hard clear.
